mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES and TRANSIT keep rising from their current troughs, weekday commuting will feed more lunch, convenience, and after-work shopping trips, pushing RETAIL_REC above its last-four-week average within four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved from -35.7 to -19.7 while TRANSIT improved from -34.4 to -30.1 in t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise above its prior 4-week mean by week 4 even though WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both increase for at least two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A rebound in PARKS to clearly positive territory diverts discretionary out-of-home time toward leisure trips and nearby purchases, so RETAIL_REC rises one to two weeks later as park visitors combine outings with shopping.
candidate_trigger: PARKS crosses above 0 after being negative the prior week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS was -7.1 at t-0w after 14.0 at t-1w and 36.3 at t-2w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC remains flat or declines over the next 14 days after PARKS turns positive again from a negative week.

mechanism_narrative: When TRANSIT stays deeply suppressed and WORKPLACES remain below baseline, city-center access is constrained and retail trips are postponed; that keeps RETAIL_REC below its last-4-week mean over the next month.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT stayed around -30 to -34 across all four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above its prior 28-day mean despite TRANSIT staying below -25 and WORKPLACES staying below -15 for most of the next four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in RESIDENTIAL time, especially when paired with weaker TRANSIT, signals more time spent near home and fewer discretionary shopping excursions, which lowers RETAIL_REC within one week.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL rises above 10 while TRANSIT remains below -25
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL stayed near 9 to 11 while TRANSIT stayed near -30 to -34
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases within 7 days after RESIDENTIAL moves above 10 and TRANSIT stays below -25.

mechanism_narrative: If GROCERY_PHARM turns persistently positive while PARKS cools from its prior surge, the same trip chains that support neighborhood errands will spill into short retail visits, lifting RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM stays above 0 for two consecutive weeks and PARKS falls from a prior local peak
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM was 0.7 at t-0w and PARKS fell from 36.3 at t-2w to -7.1 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not improve within 14 days despite GROCERY_PHARM staying positive and PARKS losing momentum.

mechanism_narrative: A continued narrowing of the gap between WORKPLACES and TRANSIT and their baseline indicates commuting normalization; that should increase retail spillovers from weekday trips and raise RETAIL_REC over four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved from -30.3 to -19.7 while TRANSIT improved from -34.4 to -30.1 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC stays below its last 4-week mean after four weeks even though both commuting proxies trend upward throughout the period.

mechanism_narrative: When PARKS drop sharply after a short-lived spike, authorities or weather-related behavior are likely suppressing discretionary outings; that same suppression spills into shopping trips and lowers RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls by more than 20 points week-on-week after being above +20
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS moved from 36.3 at t-2w to -7.1 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises or remains above its prior 14-day average after a >20-point weekly drop in PARKS.

mechanism_narrative: If GROCERY_PHARM and RESIDENTIAL both stabilize near mildly positive levels while WORKPLACES remains depressed, residents are substituting toward local essential trips rather than discretionary shopping, so RETAIL_REC stays below its prior month average over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM and RESIDENTIAL are near zero to positive while WORKPLACES remains around -20 to -36
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC exceeds its previous 28-day mean even though GROCERY_PHARM and RESIDENTIAL stay near current levels and WORKPLACES remains well below baseline.
